sources.title: Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración: Clasificación de países

sources.title: Constitution of Guatemala — Article 26 freedom of movement
sources.publisher: Congreso de la República de Guatemala
sources.officialityEvidence: Guatemala’s Congress publishes the current Constitution on its official legislative domain; Article 26 directly protects Guatemalans from being denied entry and waives visas.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No podrá ... prohibírsele la entrada al territorio nacional ... Los guatemaltecos pueden entrar y salir ... sin ... visa.

policies.title: Guatemala: named Category A ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: MINEX’s current ordinary-passport classification expressly marks these nationalities Category A, exempt from the Guatemalan visa requirement. The duplicate Andorra Category A/Category B entries are not normalized and remain unresolved.
conditions: Category A travellers enter with a valid passport, but border admission remains subject to immigration control and applicable bilateral or multilateral arrangements.
The source provides no nationality-wide short-stay duration, port, fee, return/onward travel, funds, accommodation, health, extension or admissibility rule for this policy; none is inferred.
This ordinary-passport baseline excludes residence, work, study, family, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and other special-document routes.
The Category A row for the United Kingdom includes passport-wording conditions affecting British passports connected to Hong Kong. It does not directly establish the catalog’s HKSAR passport row.

policies.title: Guatemala: named Category B ordinary passports require advance consular visa
policies.summary: MINEX’s current ordinary-passport schedule expressly marks these nationalities Category B (visa consular). IGM says Category B applicants use the nearest Guatemalan embassy; the normalized baseline is visa_required, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: A Category B tourist/traveller visa is an advance mission-consular process. IGM lists a form, valid passport, photographs, travel reservation, financial evidence, international credit card and proof of payment.

The official classification carries a conditional Category B exception for holders of a valid United States, Mexican, Canadian or Schengen visa. It depends on a third-country visa and is not a nationality-wide access policy.
Passport validity, visa grant, duration, entries, fee, extension, port, onward travel, funds and final admission remain individual or process-specific unless the authority expressly determines them.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and other special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: Guatemala: named Category C ordinary passports require advance consulted visa
policies.summary: MINEX’s current ordinary-passport schedule expressly marks these nationalities Category C (visa consultada). IGM says a Guatemalan guarantor processes it directly at IGM; the normalized baseline is visa_required, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The Category C tourist process requires advance consultation at IGM and ordinarily a form, valid passport, passport-validity certification, police/criminal-record evidence, transport ticket or Guatemalan guarantor, and payment.

IGM’s current FAQ says the United States, Mexican, Canadian or Schengen visa exception applies to Category B; Category C nationals must still obtain a Guatemalan visa. Other family, residence or document-conditioned category changes are not nationality-wide baselines.
Passport validity, visa grant, duration, entries, fee, extension, port, onward travel, funds, sponsor and final admission remain case-specific unless directly determined.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and other special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: Guatemalan citizens cannot be denied entry and do not require a visa
policies.summary: Article 26 of Guatemala’s current Constitution directly prohibits denying a Guatemalan entry to the national territory and states that Guatemalans may enter without a visa.
conditions: This policy records the direct constitutional entry right for the same-country passport relationship; passport issuance, identification, border processing and exceptional legal controls remain separate matters.

conflicts.explanation: The current MINEX ordinary-passport schedule explicitly assigns this nationality to Category B or C, which requires an advance Guatemalan visa; it is not an electronic or arrival visa.

unresolved.reason: The same current MINEX schedule gives Andorra ordinary passports both Category A (visa-exempt) and Category B (consular visa). Neither result can safely override the other without a correcting operative source.
MINEX’s United Kingdom row has document-wording rules for certain British passports connected to Hong Kong, but it does not directly classify an HKSAR ordinary passport.
Kosovo is not expressly named in the reviewed current MINEX ordinary-passport categories; omission is not used to infer an advance-visa complement.
Macao is not expressly classified as an ordinary passport nationality in the reviewed current schedules; third-country or special-document wording is not generalized.
South Sudan is not expressly named in the reviewed current MINEX ordinary-passport categories; the schedule’s Sudan row cannot be extended to it.
